question: A snail at the bottom of a 10-foot well climbs 3 feet each day and slides back 2 feet each night. Does it first reach the top on day 8?

claims.text: The snail gains a net 1 foot per full day-and-night cycle.
On the final day the snail escapes during the day and never slides back.
At the start of day 7 the snail is at 6 feet.
On day 7 the snail climbs to 9 feet, short of the top, and slides back to 7 feet overnight.
On day 8 the snail starts at 7 feet and climbs to 10 feet, reaching the top.
The snail cannot reach the top on any day earlier than day 8.
Dividing 10 by the net daily gain of 1 foot suggests day 10.
The naive day-10 shortcut is wrong because it ignores that the snail does not slide back after escaping.
The snail might be counted as reaching the top only after the night.
Reaching the top means being out of the well, so that objection does not fit the problem.
The first day the snail reaches the top is day 8.
